editorial.headline: Furniture Repair: A National Opening, a Bali PMA Bar
editorial.standfirst: Furniture repair and maintenance is nationally open to 100% foreign ownership, yet Bali’s permanent PMA moratorium means a foreign investor cannot register the activity there today.
editorial.body:
At its core, this activity is the practical craft of keeping furniture and household fittings in service. It covers repair and maintenance work on furniture and household equipment: coating, finishing, repair and restoration. The scope also reaches office furniture and the assembly of self-standing furniture. Rather than a loose furnishing label, it identifies the interventions that matter: treating a surface, completing a finish, repairing a piece or bringing it back into condition. It is as relevant to a piece’s finish as to its restoration.

Who can register is unusually clear. The activity is open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar enterprises—every scale named in the record. This broad eligibility does not alter the subject of the registration. Across that range, the work remains defined by repair and maintenance, whether it concerns a coating or finishing job, a repair or restoration, office furniture, household equipment or the assembly of self-standing furniture. Scale is an access category here, not a change to the listed activity.

Nationally, the foreign-investment position is equally direct. The activity is TERBUKA and carries a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. For a PMA company, that means full foreign ownership is allowed at the national level; there is no lower stated ceiling to navigate. The national basis recorded for that position is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. That ceiling is not a promise about a particular province, yet it is the national benchmark against which a local restriction must be read.

In Bali, the answer is more restrictive and immediate: a foreign investor cannot register this activity there today. Its Bali status is BLOCCATO_CLASSE_RISCHIO. At the Besar scale, OSS assigns Low or Medium-Low risk across every scope; Bali’s island-wide, permanent PMA moratorium blocks PMA registration for every activity classified Low or Medium-Low risk. The reason records the moratorium as of May 13, 2026. The distinction needs to remain crisp: 100% is the national foreign-ownership ceiling, while Bali blocks PMA registration for this activity. This is a jurisdictional bar, not a reduced Bali ownership percentage.
editorial.pullQuote: Nationally, the ceiling is 100%; in Bali, PMA registration for this activity is blocked.
